_help.how_to: Copy this file to game.json in your working folder, replace the example values with what the user told you, delete the example scorers, then run: python SKILL_DIR/scripts/fetch_game.py --validate game.json (SKILL.md, post-game step 1, manual path). Exit 0 means nothing to fix (a missing logo_file and a partial scorer list still exit 0); exit 3 means a WARNING to fix: fix the file or ask the user, then run it again. Record only what the user said; never invent names, assists or stats.
_help.arena: rink name as the user gives it (e.g. Kaarela 1), or empty if unknown. Never copy an example rink
_help.finish: REG, OT or SO (overtime or shootout decided the game)
_help.result: from Näädät's point of view: W, L, OTW, OTL, SOW or SOL; empty string if the game is not final
_help.us_side: home or away. The home team is listed first on the graphic. Home when the user says so or the rink starts with an entry of team.json home_arenas (prefix match: 'Kaarela' covers 'Kaarela 1' and 'Kaarela 2'); away when the user says so or names the opponent's rink; ask the user if still unclear
_help.home / away: name and goals of each team; is_us true for Näädät, false for the opponent. Swap the two blocks and set us_side to away for an away game
_help.logo_file: opponent logo file (PNG/JPG), a real file from the user or the club, path relative to the folder that holds game.json (just the file name when it sits next to game.json). Remove the key if there is no logo: the script then draws a lettered badge
_help.periods: optional; [] when the user gave no period scores. Rows look like {"label": "1", "home": 1, "away": 0}; SO for a shootout row
_help.goals: optional goal log for slide 2; leave [] if unknown (slide 2 is then skipped). Entry: {period, time 'mm:ss' elapsed game time, team 'us' or 'them', scorer {full, short, last, first}, assists [same shape], type '', 'PP', 'SH' or 'EN', score_after 'home-away'}
_help.scorers_us: Näädät scorers; goals > 0 shows them on slide 1. assists is a number, or null when unknown. A player known only by last name gets only 'last' filled and the other name fields empty (see 'Malli'). A partial list is fine when the user knows only some scorers: --validate prints a note (exit 0) and the graphic marks the list as partial. Leave [] if no scorers are known
_help.goalies: optional [{team_name, name {full, short, last, first}, saves, is_us}]; [] if unknown
